answer: Concentrated-liquidity pools charge every position its own gas and range upkeep, so splitting capital into many tiny positions loses money. Price identities the same way: each key pays a small, non-transferable upkeep per epoch in compute and must keep answering to stay in range. A sybil swarm becomes an island of dust positions bleeding fees, and the velvet promise of free multiplication turns out to be a fable once the per-key carry cost is summed.
